Calling policy: which class x state is called at which level

Source: R/caller.R
call_policy.Rd

Normal tissue: per cell, chromosomes in every state and arm / 50 Mb losses and CN-LOH are reportable; 20 Mb losses / CN-LOH and sub-chromosome gains are computed per cell but not reportable (reportable = FALSE, recall 0.24-0.74 per cell); 5 / 10 Mb tiles and sub-chromosome gains are pooled (level = "pool", every class x state reportable). Named event regions are reportable per cell. Tumour: per-cell rows (detection / clone assignment) are not reportable; the state is reported at clone level.

Usage

call_policy(mode = c("normal", "tumour"), sex = NULL)

Arguments

mode

"normal" or "tumour"

sex

"female", "male" or NULL (unknown, treated as female)

Value

data.table class, state, level (cell | pool | clone), reportable, chrx

Details

Column chrx says whether rows on chrX are reportable at that level. In normal tissue of a female (or unknown sex) chrX pools are not reportable: X-inactivation makes neighbouring cells share the active X, so allelic imbalance of chrX at neighbourhood (pool) scale is expected biology, not a copy-number event; per-cell chrX calls stay reportable. Male chrX is depth-only and its pools are reportable. Pass a policy with chrx = TRUE to override.
